newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher on electronic rebound.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher on electronic rebound.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed moderately higher on Thursday as electronic shares resumed their market bellwether role, buoyed by overnight gains by high tech stocks on Wall Street, brokers said.

Taiwan's weighted index, shrugging off a mixed performance by Hong Kong in the territory's first day of trading since its July 1 handover to Chinese communist rule, closed 30.91 points or 0.34 percent higher at 9,027.63.
But turnover was a cautious T$138 billion, the market's lightest since dipping to T$111.6 billion on June 14.
Electronics, which had plunged 5.44 percent Wednesday on hectic profit-taking, rebounded 3.29 percent on Thursday.

"Electronic shares still are considered Taiwan's leading shares. Wall Street's rise on Wednesday gave Taiwan's market some confidence for a rebound," said George Hou, fund manager for Jardine Fleming.
Brokers had thought Taiwan might benefit from a celebration rally in newly Chinese Hong Kong, but Hong Kong did not deliver. At 0420 GMT, the Hang Seng index was down 0.51 percent.
"Hong Kong's sluggishness might have thrown some caution into Taiwan, but the effect wasn't great," Hou said.
Blue-chip electronic firms comprised six of the session's 10 most traded shares.
Microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co gained T$3 to T$118. Another chipmaker, United Microelectronics, rose T$3.5 to T$109.5.
Other major sectors saw lacklustre performance. The heavily weighted financials eased 0.47 percent, plastics tumbled 1.40 percent and textiles dropped 0.78 percent.
"The index has hit resistance, so it seems like (a pattern): if electronics rise, the others fall, and vice versa," said Wang Jieh, analyst for Foremost Investment.
